4. `Animated.event` driven from scroll delivers the offset of the frame it is reporting, not the previous one — [core#52657](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/52657).
5. No animated property update is lost when a commit lands in the same frame; the merge order of commit-versus-animation is stated and tested.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Unit (C++):** an injected clock steps the graph; at each tick the value seen by every consumer is asserted equal, including across commit boundaries. Inside the 100% line-and-branch gate.
- **TSan:** the frame thread stepping the graph concurrently with mounting transactions, clean.
- **E2E:** a bundle animating a transform while `--inject-pointer` presses at the painted position on scripted frames, with the ordered event trace compared to a committed expectation — the assertion that fails on upstream today.

## Related

Definition-of-done for #19 (native-driven animations). Pairs with #74 (unmounted targets) and #75 (Animated value conformance), and with the animated hit-testing issue in this batch. Belongs to the animation programme in #95 if that plan supersedes M2 placement.

issues.title: test(animation): the native-driver style allowlist is enforced at the boundary
issues.body:
**Priority P2** — cheap to encode, and it converts a class of runtime surprises into a startup-time error message; it is also the natural home for the interpolation edge cases upstream keeps rediscovering.

## Context

- [core#40973](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/40973) — "Style property `marginLeft` is not supported by the native animated module": the allowlist exists, it is enforced at runtime, and it reaches the user as a thrown error with no guidance.
- [core#36608](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/36608) — `Animated.Value.interpolate` yields `NaN` for radian outputs: a unit-carrying output range that the interpolator does not model.
- [core#34022](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34022) — an iOS crash when a colour interpolation runs on the native driver.
- [core#37900](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/37900) — open: `Animated` tracking with the native driver does not work as expected.
- [core#37061](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/37061) — `AnimatedInterpolation` and `AnimatedModulo` never call their listeners.
- [core#49719](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/49719) — 16 comments: listeners never fire on values built from `Animated` operators.

## What to verify

1. The set of properties our native driver can animate is enumerated in **one** place, is the same set the JS side advertises, and a property outside it produces a clear diagnostic naming the property and the alternative — not a crash and not silence.
2. Interpolation output types are modelled: numbers, units (`deg`, `rad`, `%`), and colours, each with a defined behaviour for out-of-range inputs. `NaN` never leaves the interpolator — the #73 rule applied to animation.
3. Every node type the graph supports (value, interpolation, modulo, diffClamp, addition/multiplication/division, tracking) calls its listeners and propagates to its parents — [core#37061](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/37061), [core#49719](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/49719).
4. Colour interpolation runs without a platform-specific crash path — [core#34022](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34022).
5. The allowlist is derived from the renderer's actual capability rather than hand-maintained: adding a paintable animated property updates it, and a test fails if the two drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Unit (C++/TS):** the node-type table and the interpolation table asserted, including non-finite and out-of-range inputs, inside the 100% gates.
- The diagnostic text for a rejected property is asserted, so it stays actionable.
- The allowlist-versus-renderer drift check runs in CI.

## Related

Extends #75 (Animated value conformance: units, percentages, interpolation, additive composition). Applies #73's boundary rule. Under #19 and the animation programme in #95.

issues.title: test(animation): LayoutAnimation — decide it, then prove it or refuse it
issues.body:
**Priority P2** — a legacy API that upstream's own New Architecture has been visibly failing to carry for three years; declining it is a legitimate outcome, but it has to be a decision with a diagnostic rather than an omission with a silent no-op.

## Context

- [core#47617](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/47617) — **open**, 26 reactions: `LayoutAnimation.configureNext()` is broken in 0.76. The most-reacted animation issue in the era.
- [core#38661](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/38661) — **open since 2023**, 28 comments: "[New Architecture] LayoutAnimation Breaking".
- [core#46568](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/46568) — 20 comments: LayoutAnimations crash under a new iOS SDK on the new architecture.
- [core#33740](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/33740) — `LayoutAnimation.create()` completely non-functional on Android.
- [core#48722](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/48722) — a border-radius artifact (black background) during a layout animation.
- [core#49958](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/49958) — `LayoutAnimationController` leaks memory.
- [core#50442](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/50442) — closed, `Resolution: Fixed`, 18 reactions: a Modal's children render in the **top-left corner** for the first few frames. Not `LayoutAnimation`, but the same class: a node painted before its layout is known.

The API's shape is the problem: it asks the mounting layer to animate *between two committed trees*, which requires the mounting layer to hold both and interpolate — exactly what Fabric's mounting transaction is not built to do, and exactly why Reanimated 4 reimplements it.

## What to verify

1. Decide: implement `LayoutAnimation` over our mounting transactions, defer it to the Reanimated-layer decision in the animation programme (#95), or refuse it. Record the decision in `docs/cpp-toolchain.md` and in ADR terms if it changes ADR-0001's animation stance.
2. If refused: `LayoutAnimation.configureNext` produces a single clear warning per call site and the layout change applies instantly — never a partially animated, never a dropped frame.
3. If implemented: an interrupted layout animation (a second commit mid-animation) resolves to the newest tree without residue, and the controller's resources are released when the animation ends or is interrupted — [core#49958](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/49958).
4. Either way: no node is ever painted at a default position before its layout is known — the [core#50442](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/50442) first-frame rule, which applies to our overlay work in #62 regardless of this decision.

## Acceptance criteria

- The decision is written down with this issue number before any code lands.
- **Unit (C++):** the chosen behaviour asserted, including the interrupted case if implemented, inside the 100% gate.
- **Golden/E2E:** the first-frame rule (point 4) proven by a frame captured at mount, since it holds under every outcome.

## Related

Under #19 and the animation programme in #95. The first-frame rule is shared with #62 (Modal and overlay surfaces) and #46 (ScrollView content size on the first frame).

issues.title: perf(animation): a native-driver frame-cost gate
issues.body:
**Priority P1** — upstream shipped a 20× animation regression to a stable release and a user found it; a 120 fps demo is a stated M2 deliverable, and a demo without a gate is a screenshot.

## Context

- [core#50716](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/50716) — closed, `Resolution: Fixed`, 20 reactions: "Animation is **20× slower** in New Architecture", with two branches of the same app as the repro. It shipped, and CI did not catch it.
- [core#44514](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/44514) — `useNativeDriver` performance regression in 0.74 on the new architecture, compared against list scrolling.
- [core#47490](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/47490) — closed, **60 reactions**, 134 comments: "Performance issues with Bridgeless" — the most-reacted new-architecture issue of the era.
- [core#34583](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34583) — 18 reactions: an app **freezes** when animations run inside an inverted list.
- [core#38470](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/38470) — open: scrolling a list whose content is moving stutters or blocks entirely.

Our side: #20 owns pacing, `wp_presentation` measurement and Tracy; #59 owns frame-source liveness. Neither states a cost budget for the animation step itself, and ADR-0001 puts that step on a thread whose deadline is the compositor's.

## What to verify

1. A per-frame budget for the animation step (graph evaluation + property application + damage), stated as a number, measured with `wp_presentation` feedback rather than wall clock, at 60 Hz and 120 Hz.
2. The budget holds with N concurrent animated nodes for a stated N, and degrades predictably beyond it rather than collapsing.
3. Animating while a list scrolls stays inside the budget — the [core#34583](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/34583)/[core#38470](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/38470) combination.
4. No animation frame allocates on the frame thread — a zero-allocation assertion, since allocation is the mechanism behind most of the regressions above.
5. The numbers are uploaded as CI artifacts and a regression beyond the stated threshold fails the build.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Perf/E2E:** the animation scenarios run under the headless compositor with p95 frame time asserted against the 8.33 ms budget and the animation-step budget asserted separately, per the testing gospel.
- **Unit (C++):** the zero-allocation assertion on the frame-thread path with an injected allocator, inside the 100% gate.
- A scenario reproducing [core#50716](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/50716)'s shape (a simple continuously animating view) is in the gate permanently, because that is the one that shipped.

## Related

Extends #20 (pacing, VRR, Tracy) and #59 (frame-source liveness). Under #19; belongs to the animation programme in #95 if that supersedes M2 placement. Shares the allocation discipline with the mounting-ceiling issue in this batch.

issues.title: test(core): every commit terminates, and every mounting transaction is atomic
issues.body:
**Priority P0** — these are bugs in code that is already compiled into `rnl_window`; they reach us by linkage, not by analogy, and one of them is an unbounded retry on the thread that draws.

## Context

Upstream's Fabric-era corpus contains a cluster of `ReactCommon` defects reported against iOS and Android only because those are the only places it runs:

- [core#51870](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/51870) — `[Starvation] Assertion failed: (attempts < 1024), function commit, file ShadowTree.cpp`. A commit loop that does not converge; the assertion is the only thing that stops it.
- [core#52373](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/52373) — open, 8 reactions: the intermediate state of a `useLayoutEffect` can be mounted by **a commit from a different thread**.
- [core#44111](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/44111) — closed, `Resolution: Fixed`, 14 reactions: UI updates made from a layout effect are flushed in a *separate* transaction, producing a visible intermediate frame.
- [core#49077](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/49077) — **open, 49 reactions, 85 comments**: "Unable to find viewState for tag N. Surface stopped: false" — a mounting instruction referencing a node whose state has gone.
- [core#49694](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/49694) — closed, 55 reactions: a C++ state update is not received when a path-cloning commit hook is used.
- [core#47576](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/47576) — native view **commands** timed incorrectly relative to mounting.
- [core#41699](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/41699) — a `ComponentDescriptor::adopt` signature change breaking every third-party component.

Our configuration sharpens two of them: our commit runs on a thread we own, so [core#52373](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/52373)'s cross-thread mounting is our default rather than an edge case; and `LinuxMountingManager::dispatchCommand` is empty, so [core#47576](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/47576)'s ordering question is unanswered rather than answered wrongly.

## What to verify

1. Termination: a commit with a re-entrant state update converges within a bounded number of attempts; exceeding the bound is a diagnostic and a dropped update, never an assertion or an infinite loop.
2. Atomicity: the tree produced by one React render pass, including layout-effect updates, is mounted in **one** transaction — no intermediate frame shows a half-updated tree ([core#44111](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/44111)).
3. Identity: every mounting instruction references a node present in the scene; a missing tag is a test failure with the tag and the transaction in the message, not a silent skip ([core#49077](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/49077)).
4. `dispatchCommand` is ordered relative to mounting: a command issued in the same render pass as a mount is delivered after that mount, and this is asserted rather than assumed ([core#47576](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/47576)).
5. A state update originating on a non-JS thread is serialized against commits; TSan-clean.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Unit (C++):** re-entrant-commit, layout-effect-update, missing-tag and command-ordering scenarios driven through the real `ShadowTree`/`MountingCoordinator` path with upstream assertions live (`NDEBUG` off), inside the 100% gate.
- **TSan:** concurrent commit and mount, clean.
- **E2E:** a frame-by-frame capture proving no intermediate frame for a layout-effect update.
- The suite re-runs on every React Native version bump as part of #58's drift oracle, since the code under test is vendored.

## Related

Follows #10 (Fabric bootstrap) and #12 (retained scene). Feeds #58 (upstream-parity conformance) and #77 (cross-thread contract stress). Shares the mutation table with the measure-callback issue in this batch.

issues.title: perf(core): per-view mounting cost, measured
issues.body:
**Priority P1** — upstream's mounting cost regressed to ~1 ms per view and stayed there through a stable release; the flagship app mounts a 81-cell board plus chrome in one transaction, so this number is directly on our critical path.

## Context

- [core#51869](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/51869) — closed, `Resolution: Fixed`, **44 reactions**, 27 comments: "[Performance] Mounting is very slow on Android (almost 1 ms per one view)". A 200-node screen therefore costs 200 ms of mounting.
- [core#47490](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/47490) — closed, 60 reactions, 134 comments: bridgeless performance, the umbrella the above sits under.
- [core#36296](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/36296) — 46 reactions, 171 comments: very long re-rendering times after a minor bump.
- [core#57198](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/issues/57198) — open: memory not reclaimed across repeated mount/unmount cycles.

Our side: `docs/cpp-toolchain.md` records that the damage walk runs the same snapshot code over a subtree per mutation and that every snapshot copies the attributed string; #20 will provide the reporting surface, but no number exists yet for what a mounting transaction costs.

## What to verify

1. A stated per-view mounting cost budget and a stated total for a first mount of N nodes, measured on the commit and render threads separately.
2. The cost is linear in the number of *mutations*, not in the size of the tree: appending one node to a 2,000-node tree costs the same as appending it to a 20-node tree.
3. Snapshot copying is bounded: a text-heavy subtree does not re-copy attributed strings for unaffected siblings.
4. The numbers are produced by the same instrumentation #20 uses, uploaded as CI artifacts, and a regression beyond a stated threshold fails the build.
5. The measurement scenario includes the flagship's real shape (a grid of ~100 interactive cells) rather than a synthetic tree only.

## Acceptance criteria

- **Perf/E2E:** mounting scenarios under the headless compositor with per-transaction timings recorded via `wp_presentation` feedback and Tracy zones, asserted against the budget.
- **Unit (C++):** the linearity property (point 2) asserted with mutation counts and an injected clock, inside the 100% gate.
- Numbers are tracked over time, per the gospel's "numbers are tracked, not vibed" rule.

## Related

Extends #20 (pacing and Tracy) and #12 (damage tracking). Pairs with the allocation-ceiling issue in this batch and with #24 (flagship bring-up), which supplies the realistic scenario.
